read.instructionDe: Lesen Sie die Nachricht. Tippen Sie auf ein Wort für seine Bedeutung.
read.instructionEn: Read the message. Tap a word for its meaning.
read.text:
Hallo Ana!
Heute ist Mittwoch und ich bin krank.
Um sechs Uhr aufstehen? Heute nicht!
Mein Termin beim Arzt ist um halb zehn.
Hast du am Donnerstag Zeit?
Nachmittags um Viertel nach vier bin ich frei.
Ist die Uhrzeit gut für dich?
Ich komme nicht zu spät: Mein Wecker ist gut!
Viele Grüße, Lena

questions.promptDe: Wann ist Lenas Termin beim Arzt? Wählen Sie die Antwort.
questions.promptEn: When is Lena’s appointment at the doctor’s? Choose the answer.
questions.explanationDe: In der Nachricht steht: Der Termin beim Arzt ist um halb zehn. Halb zehn ist 9.30 Uhr.
questions.explanationEn: The message says the appointment is at “halb zehn”. That is 9.30: half an hour before ten.

questions.promptDe: Wann hat Lena am Donnerstag Zeit? Wählen Sie die Antwort.
questions.promptEn: When does Lena have time on Thursday? Choose the answer.
options: In the afternoon, at a quarter past four.
In the afternoon, at a quarter to four.
In the evening, at a quarter past eight.
questions.answer: In the afternoon, at a quarter past four.
questions.explanationDe: In der Nachricht steht: Nachmittags um Viertel nach vier ist Lena frei. Das ist 16.15 Uhr.
questions.explanationEn: The message says Lena is free in the afternoon at “Viertel nach vier”: a quarter past four.

meaning.promptDe: Was macht Lena um sechs Uhr? Wählen Sie die Antwort.
meaning.promptEn: What does Lena do at six o’clock? Choose the answer.

meaning.promptDe: Wann ist der Termin von Lena? Wählen Sie die Antwort.
meaning.promptEn: When is Lena’s appointment? Choose the answer.
options: On Monday at a quarter past eight.
On Tuesday at a quarter to eight.
On Monday at a quarter to eight.
meaning.answer: On Monday at a quarter to eight.

meaning.promptDe: Kommt Lena heute pünktlich? Wählen Sie die Bedeutung.
meaning.promptEn: Will Lena be on time today? Choose the meaning.
options: No, she is running late today.
Yes, she is always on time.
No, her alarm clock is broken.
meaning.answer: Yes, she is always on time.

meaning.promptDe: Wann ist Lena am Dienstag frei? Wählen Sie die Antwort.
meaning.promptEn: When is Lena free on Tuesday? Choose the answer.

meaning.promptDe: Was sagt Lena über den Mittwoch? Wählen Sie die Bedeutung.
meaning.promptEn: What does Lena say about Wednesday? Choose the meaning.

notes: Chunks are the five question-answer pairs of the dialogue; no boundary was in doubt.

Both speakers (Ana, Lena) are learner roles here, so every line is eligible for say. I kept say off the two dictation lines (hoeren.lines 3 and 7): chunks 2 and 4 therefore say Ana's question (lines 2 and 6), which is the first line of its chunk and so has no cue line on the say screen (SceneStage shows a cue only if an earlier line of the same chunk exists). If a cue matters more than keeping the dictation unrehearsed, switch them to lines 3 and 7; the validator accepts both.

Read text: a message from Lena, written on the Wednesday of her doctor's appointment (dialogue line 9: „Am Mittwoch beim Arzt“). It continues the dialogue: Ana asked about Thursday and got no answer; the message offers Thursday afternoon. It carries all seven Wortfeld entries the dialogue lacks (Uhrzeit, Zeit, zu spät, halb, Viertel nach, aufstehen, krank).

aufstehen was the hard one: the gloss finder needs the infinitive, and without modal verbs (A1.2) an infinitive has few natural homes. It stands in the elliptical „Um sechs Uhr aufstehen? Heute nicht!“, which is ordinary chat German and picks up dialogue line 1.
„Ist die Uhrzeit gut für dich?“ is correct but plainer than what a native would text („Passt dir die Uhrzeit?“); passen is not taught.
The first read question tests the Lektion's own trap (halb zehn = 9.30, not 10.30).

Existing data: der Abend is in the Wortfeld but in no dialogue line as a noun; the checker counts it as covered only because lineFor() finds the substring „abend“ inside „abends“ (line 7). I did not add it to the read text because the checker does not ask for it; say if you want it in.
Existing data: the dialogue is titled „Wann hast du Zeit?“ but neither Zeit nor Uhrzeit occurs in any line; both now occur in the read text only.
Phonetik: all three items are sentence-melody items (W-Frage, falling), not word-stress items, so the sound stage is pending for L8. Not changed.

PROOF (added 2026-11-14): four tasks, one per can-do, in can-do order. The German prompts are cue dialogues („Sie: …“) without an instruction verb, because RULE 35 holds promptDe to the taught-word horizon and fragen, sagen, antworten and Satz are untaught; the English twin carries the instruction, and on the German-only toggle the can-do line above the prompt does. The partner is „Ihre Freundin“ or „eine Frau“, not Lena (see engine limit 3).

Proof goal 0 (ask and say the time): two parts. Question: „Wie spät ist es?“ or „Wie viel Uhr ist es?“, each also after „Entschuldigung, “ and before „, bitte“. Time for 10:30 in words: „(Es ist) halb elf.“, „(Es ist) zehn Uhr dreißig.“, „Es ist zehn dreißig.“ Digits are refused on purpose (the cue says „ohne Zahlen“). LIMIT, re-teach: no dialogue line asks or tells the time, so the pointer is the Wortfeld entry „halb“ (index 6, „halb neun = 8.30“). It re-teaches the time only. The question is reachable in the re-teach card only through the collapsed number/clock reference (FULL_HOUR rule: „Wie spät ist es? Es ist neun Uhr, ohne um.“), which SetReference adds because the task text contains „Uhr“. A dialogue line or Wortfeld entry with „Wie spät ist es?“ would close this gap.

Proof goal 1 (arrange an appointment): one part. The friend asks when the appointment is; the cue gives „Freitag, 9 Uhr“ as data and the learner names day and clock time: „Der Termin ist / Unser Termin ist / Er ist / (nothing) + am Freitag um neun Uhr“, day and time in either order, the hour as „neun Uhr“, „neun“, „9 Uhr“ or „9“, the three other word orders pool item extra-a11-l08-08 accepts, and offering the slot („Am Freitag um neun Uhr habe ich Zeit.“, „Ich bin am Freitag um neun Uhr frei.“). Re-teach: dialogue line 3 (zero-based), which has to be adapted to the new day and time. LIMIT: the dialogue never fixes an appointment (Ana only asks, Lena only says when she is busy or free), so „vereinbaren“ is proven as naming day and clock time with am and um, not as a negotiation. A proposal question („Hast du am Freitag Zeit?“) stands in the read text only and has no dialogue line to re-teach it; Ana’s own line 6 is two sentences („Und am Dienstag? Bist du nachmittags frei?“), and a one-part task cannot accept that shape next to the one-sentence form.

Proof goal 2 (talk about my day): one part, „Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.“ from the cue „aufstehen – wann? Ihr Wecker: 7 Uhr“; also with morgens and/or immer, with the time or „Morgens“ in first place, and the hour as „sieben Uhr“, „sieben“, „7 Uhr“ or „7“. The cue ends „Sie: Ich …“, so a bare „Um sieben Uhr.“ fails: the can-do is the sentence with the separated verb. Re-teach: dialogue line 1 (six o’clock there, seven here).

Proof goal 3 (say when I have time): one part. The week is given as data („Montag bis Freitag Arbeit. Aber Donnerstag: abends frei!“). Accepted with the time of day („abends“, „am Abend“) or with the day alone, with frei sein, Zeit haben or frei haben, day first or „Ich“ first, and the short „Am Donnerstag (abends).“ Re-teach: dialogue line 7, the same pattern on another day.

Proof, decisions to confirm: (a) A weekday without am („Ich habe Donnerstag Zeit.“, „Der Termin ist Freitag um neun Uhr.“, a bare „Donnerstag.“) is refused although colloquial German allows it, because „Wochentag mit am“ is this Lektion’s rule; adding those forms would reverse it. (b) „Ich stehe auf um sieben Uhr.“ is refused: the verb bracket is the taught form. (c) „Am Donnerstagabend …“ cannot be accepted: RULE 35 reports „Donnerstagabend“ as untaught.

Proof, limits of the engine that hold for every task of this Lektion: (1) A standalone „Entschuldigung!“, „Danke!“ or „Guten Tag!“ before or after the answer counts as an extra sentence and fails. proofTasks() takes the free courtesies from this Lektion’s Wortfeld only (src/lib/lesson/proof.js, `courtesies`), and Danke, Bitte and Entschuldigung are Lektion 1 entries, so here none is free. (2) Any other extra sentence fails as well, also a correct one. (3) A name added to the answer fails („Lena, …“, „…, Paul?“, „Herr Schmidt, …“); the engine removes only a final „, Herr/Frau X“ of a titled speaker of this dialogue. So the prompts use partners without a name. (4) A dot inside a clock time („9.00 Uhr“) splits the answer into two sentences. (5) The notice cannot be a re-teach pointer: its bodyDe fails RULE 35’s word horizon. (6) By microphone the engine scores against the one canonical `answer`, so another accepted form may score low when spoken (read from ProofStage.jsx and answerProof(), not tested). Because of (4) the prompts of this Lektion write „9 Uhr“, „7 Uhr“ and „10:30“.

Existing data: „Wie spät ist es?“ (first act of can-do 0) occurs in pretest.model, in notice.bodyEn and in the Phonetik items (whose sound stage is pending), but in no dialogue line, Wortfeld entry, read line or pool item of Lektion 8; notice.bodyDe does not have it either. pretest.accepted also lets „Wann“ and „Um wie viel Uhr“ open a question for the time of day; those ask when something happens, not what time it is.
